It is not possible to talk about tourism: It is impossible to talk about tourism in Russia without starting with the capital, Moscow, the city that never sleeps and combines the atmosphere of history with the splendour of modernity. It is a city brimming with energy and filled with monuments that tell stories of a glorious past.
Moscow's Red Quarter is the historical a: Red Square and the historic centre around it form the historical and spiritual heart of the city, and an essential stop for any Arab visitor. It is not just a square, but an open-air museum that tells the great history of Russia. Here, the grandeur of Russian architecture is on show at its finest, and the famous monuments that have long adorned postcards and film scenes stand side by side. A visit to Red Square begins in front of St Basil’s Cathedral, famous for its colourful domes and unique design resembling a rising flame, an unmistakable symbol of Moscow. This cathedral is an architectural masterpiece dating back to the sixteenth century, and its interior details are no less magnificent than its exterior.
On the other side of the square stands t: On the other side of the square stands the majestic Kremlin, a historic fortress of palaces, churches and government buildings that is the seat of Russian government. Visitors can explore the Kremlin’s squares and historic churches, such as the Assumption Cathedral and the Archangel Cathedral, and visit the Armoury Chamber, which displays treasures of jewellery, historical weapons and luxurious tsarist carriages. Lenin’s Mausoleum is also located on Red Square, and is a historical landmark for those wishing to delve deeper into Russia’s modern history.
As you stroll through the square, you'll: As you stroll through the square, you’ll notice GUM, a luxurious historic department store overlooking the square with its stunning 19th-century glass design. It is not just a place for shopping; it is a landmark in itself that combines architectural elegance with a unique shopping experience. The square is busy with visitors and locals alike, and its atmosphere changes with the seasons, becoming a festive space in winter, decorated with lights and holiday markets, and a lively place to relax in summer. Spending time in Red Square is an enriching experience that touches the soul, feeds the mind and offers a profound glimpse into Russian identity.
Do not miss the opportunity to ride the: Do not miss the opportunity to ride the Moscow Metro, known as the “underground palaces” thanks to its stations decorated with beautiful Russian art, including mosaics, huge chandeliers and exquisite sculptures. Each station is a masterpiece in itself and worth discovering.
For arts lovers, the Bolshoi Theater is: For arts lovers, the Bolshoi Theatre is a must-visit. Watch a ballet or opera at this legendary theatre and experience classical Russian art at its finest. The theatre’s architecture and long history make it an outstanding cultural landmark.
Old Arbat Street is one of Moscow's olde: Old Arbat Street is one of Moscow’s oldest and liveliest streets, and is pedestrian-only. You can wander along it to enjoy traditional shops and modern cafés, and watch artists and musicians display their talents. It’s a great place to buy souvenirs and get a taste of the local atmosphere.
For a stunning panoramic view of Moscow,: For a stunning panoramic view of Moscow, head to the Sparrow Hills. From here, you can see the Kremlin, the Cathedral of Christ the Saviour and modern skyscrapers in a scene that combines the charm of the old city with the glamour of modernity. The famous Moscow State University is also located there.

The best time to visit Russia depends la: The best time to visit Russia depends largely on your interests and what you want to experience, as Russia has a different beauty in every season, making it a year-round destination with many faces.
Summer is the most popular season to vis: Summer is the most popular season to visit Russia, especially Moscow and St Petersburg. The weather is mild and warm, and the days are very long, allowing more time to explore the sights and parks. In St Petersburg, you can enjoy the magical phenomenon of the “White Nights”, when the sun never sets completely and the city remains bathed in twilight throughout the night, creating a romantic and unique atmosphere. Many festivals and outdoor events take place during this time, and the fountains at Peterhof Palace are at their most beautiful. However, prices may be higher and destinations more crowded.
Spring is a beautiful time to visit Russ: Spring is a beautiful time to visit Russia, as the snow begins to melt, flowers bloom, and the cities turn green. The weather is mild, and it is less crowded than in summer, making for a quieter experience. May is particularly pleasant, with Victory Day (9 May) celebrations including impressive military parades in Moscow’s Red Square.
Autumn is another great time to visit, e: Autumn is another great time to visit, especially for nature lovers. The foliage turns golden and red, creating stunning landscapes, especially in gardens and parks. The weather is breezy and slightly cool, and the crowds are noticeably smaller than in summer. This is an ideal time for cultural visits to museums, galleries and theatres, as the cultural season is in full swing.
For those looking for an authentic and u: For those looking for an authentic and unique Russian experience, winter has a special charm. Cities are covered in snow, and the landscape turns into a fairy-tale world. Christmas and New Year markets are held, and the cities are lit up with festive lights, creating a magical atmosphere. You can try ice skating in public squares, such as Red Square, and enjoy hot drinks. Despite the extreme cold, a warm welcome awaits indoors in museums, cafés and theatres. This period is ideal for enjoying the splendour of Russian ballet in its traditional setting, and for experiencing the authentic Russian winter so often celebrated in novels.
In general, if you prefer warm and long: In general, if you prefer warm weather and long days, summer is the best choice. If you are looking for a peaceful cultural experience and natural beauty, spring and autumn are ideal. For lovers of adventure and winter beauty, nothing compares to the magic of snow-covered Russia.

To ensure a smooth and enjoyable travel: To ensure a smooth and enjoyable trip to Russia, especially for Arab travellers, here are some important tips to help you settle in and enjoy every moment:
Russian is the official language, and no: Russian is the official language, and not everyone may speak English, especially outside major cities. It is recommended to download translation apps on your phone (such as Google Translate) and use the voice or camera translation mode to translate signs and menus.
Learn some basic Russian phrases like \": Learning some basic Russian phrases like “Hello” (Привет – Privet), “Thank you” (Спасибо – Spasibo), “Please” (Пожалуйста – Pozhaluysta), “Yes/No” (Да/Нет – Da/Net), “How much?” (Сколько стоит? – Skol’ko stoit?) will show respect for the country’s culture and make everyday interactions easier.
Russians are a fairly conservative peopl: Russians are fairly reserved people who value respect and courtesy. A smile and an attempt to communicate in their language make a big difference.
In Moscow and St. Petersburg, options fo: In Moscow and St Petersburg, the number of restaurants serving halal food is growing, especially in neighbourhoods with large Muslim communities. You can look for them in advance using restaurant apps or Google Maps.
If you have difficulty finding halal foo: If you have difficulty finding halal food, fish, seafood and vegetarian dishes are widely available in most restaurants. Traditional Russian dishes such as borscht (soup) and salads are often safe choices.
Take advantage of the efficient and beau: Take advantage of the efficient and beautiful metro system in Moscow and St Petersburg. Metro maps are available in Russian and English at major stations.
As in any large tourist city, be wary of: As in any large tourist city, be wary of pickpockets, especially in crowded places and on public transport. Keep your valuables in a safe place.
In general, Russia is safe for tourists. However, it is advisable to avoid wandering around deserted areas at night, and to check the reputation of any place before visiting it.
The official currency is the Russian rub: The official currency is the Russian rouble. Be sure to carry enough roubles in cash, as Visa and Mastercard cards issued outside Russia are not accepted, even in the larger cities.
